thread:
marta: quick flag: after deploying q4-quant for orion-retriever on staging, our multilingual retrieval recall@10 dropped notably for ja/zh queries. small repro + a weird example where a Japanese query matches an unrelated English doc. anyone seen quantization affect embedding alignment like this?

marta: repro command (embedding + faiss rebuild):
```
./embed_and_index --model=orion-retriever --quant=q4 --corpus=multi-corp-2026 \
  --locales=ja,zh,en --index=faiss_hnsw --metric=ip --norm=true 
./eval_retrieval --index=faiss_hnsw --queries=multi-queries-2026 --k=10 --metric=recall
```

marta: quick numbers (float32 -> q4):
```
locale  recall@10 (float)  recall@10 (q4)
ja      0.842              0.663
zh      0.811              0.612
en      0.871              0.854
```
marta: note: English mostly stable, CJK hit much larger.

cheng: curious. did you re-normalize after quantized embeddings? q4 path sometimes returns slightly different L2 norms pre-normalize which can change ip ordering if normalization isn't applied consistently.

marta: yes normalizing applied both times. dug into per-query nearest neighbor ids for a failing ja query:
```
query (ja): "\u660e\u65e5\u306b\u958b\u50ac\u3055\u308c\u308b\u30a4\u30d9\u30f3\u30c8\u306e\u53d6\u5f97\u30ab\u30fc\u30c9\u306b\u3064\u3044\u3066\u8a73\u3057\u304f\u306f\u2026"
float nn0_id -> doc_jp_023  (exact match, high score)
q4   nn0_id -> doc_en_981   (unrelated english doc, similar short token like "Event" in en)
```

oliver: that smells like tokenization drift or embedding table remap. quantizer might be reassigning subtoken ids in the lower precision path when we reconstruct input token ids for the embedder. can you run tokenize-diff between float and q4 bundle for that query?

marta: ran tokenize-diff:
```
float tokenize("\u660e\u65e5\u306b\u958b\u50ac\u3055\u308c\u308b\u30a4\u30d9\u30f3\u30c8") -> ["\u660e\u65e5\u306b","\u958b\u50ac","\u3055\u308c\u308b","\u30a4\u30d9\u30f3\u30c8"]
q4   tokenize("\u660e\u65e5\u306b\u958b\u50ac\u3055\u308c\u308b\u30a4\u30d9\u30f3\u30c8") -> ["\u660e", "", "\u65e5\u306b", "\u958b", "\u50ac", "\u3055\u308c", "\u308b", "\u30a4", "\u30d9", "\u30c8"]
```

marta: q4 run inserts empty token and breaks multi-char tokens into singles. that will lead to different token-id sequences and hence different embedding output.

yara: packaging check: model-bundle hash matches across float and q4 images but runtime tokenizers differ (float used tokenizers@2.2.0, q4 image tokenizers@2.0.8). bundler didn't pin runtime.

oliver: that explains CJK-specialized tokens being split. English mostly unaffected because whitespace tokenization dominates.

cheng: immediate mitigations: (1) prevent index rebuild with mismatched tokenizer (fail if bundle tokenizer checksum != runtime), (2) add an evaluation step that compares tokenized id sequences for a sample set before indexing and blocks canary if mismatch > threshold, (3) short-term: reindex with float runtime tokenizers in the q4 image as a stopgap.

deploy-bot: Canary index-build started: rollout_id=rl-2026-2011, hosts=3/3 updated, metadata: tokenizers/hash: a1b2c3 -> d4e5f6. See `deploy-bot logs rl-2026-2011` for details.

marta: i'll open GH issue with failing query, tokenize diffs, and the index nearest-neighbor dumps. adding unit checks for token-id equality pre-indexing.

oliver: long-term: model bundler should embed a deterministic tokenizer runtime + a token-id mapping table used by the embedder. if quant path changes IDs we need a stable mapping layer.

marta: agreed. for now i'm rolling back the q4 canary index and reindexing with float tokenizers to restore CJK recall while infra teams fix bundler. will post recovered numbers here once done. :pray:
